title: MARS-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory MARS-Seq schematic, interpreted as the single-cell mRNA counting architecture identified with Jaitin et al. (PMID 24531970). One linear path runs from polyadenylated RNA through a labeled DNA intermediate and amplified RNA to a P5/P7 cDNA library. Initial RT, pooling of lysate contents, and the unlabeled in vitro transcription bridge are included only where the supplied text makes them architecturally necessary. This is not a reconstruction of unshown protocol settings or a later MARS-Seq version.

states.label: Polyadenylated mRNA from individual single-cell lysates
features: Biological target is the sampled cellular mRNA pool; chemical input is RNA with a depicted AA(A)n tail.
FACS isolation and lysis in individual wells are supplied text context, not drawn compartments.
The yellow outline has no legend or attachment symbol and is not interpreted as a bead, surface or compartment.

evidence.locator: Far left: yellow-outlined purple RNA body ending AA(A)n; title Massively parallel RNA single-cell sequencing framework (MARS-Seq).
Description, sentences on FACS and cell lysis
evidence.quote: Single cells are first isolated into individual wells using FACS. Each cell is lysed, and the 3' ends of mRNAs are annealed to unique molecular identifiers containing a T7 promoter.

states.label: P5/P7-ended barcoded cDNA sequencing library
features: Final cDNA icon contains P5 at left and P7 at right with the orange partial-read region and colored insert/label segments between them.

The primary paper reports molecular, cellular and plate tags for multiplexed molecule counting. In combination with RNA-derived sequence, the readout supports cell-associated mRNA molecule counts and transcriptional profiles; the diagram specifies no read allocation for these components.

Poly(A)-targeted initiation and the tag-bearing end representation support a 3′-associated expression readout, not complete sequence coverage of every RNA species or full-length isoform reconstruction.
Molecule counting concerns captured and sequenced molecules; complete transcript capture or perfect molecular-label uniqueness is not established by this drawing.
The diagram provides no sequencing or analysis block, exact strand read orientation, or additional library branch.

method_scopes.rationale: The title expands MARS-Seq as a massively parallel RNA single-cell sequencing framework: this is one method, not an additional alias-defined version. All depicted operations belong to the single route. Initial RT, pooling, and IVT are explicitly marked text-supported interfaces. The original primary article establishes single-cell pooled labeled processing and three-tier counting; detailed T7 chemistry is corroborated here by the supplied review and catalogue, not by inspected original supplementary methods. The similar-method list and TruSeq product mention establish neither additional depicted variants nor equivalence or historical-development edges.

corrections.diagram_observation: The paired-strand stage is captioned Second strand synthesis. Its next arrow is labeled DNaseI and leads into RNA fragmentation; there is no labeled transcription operation. The red/green terminal colors continue in the RNA and cDNA illustrations.
corrections.primary_statement: The inspected original MARS-Seq main article identifies the method and refers to figures S1 to S6 and Supplementary methods (21); its supplied main text does not establish the reaction order at this missing label. A primary-source correction therefore remains unverified. The inspected full-text review (PMID 27198714), a secondary source, explicitly reports T7/oligo(dT)-based RT and linear amplification by IVT for MARS-Seq; its Figure 4(c) places cRNA production after second-strand cDNA synthesis. The catalogue independently states DNA transcription to RNA followed by DNA-template digestion. Operation o_ivt retains that catalogue- and review-supported bridge, clearly marked as unlabeled in the image. The keep_unresolved disposition applies to verification against the original implementation methods, not to the separately supported schematic bridge; no primary-verified chemistry or inspection of the original supplementary protocol is claimed.

unknowns.question: Where are the cellular and plate barcodes installed and read, and does the green region retained after IVT stand for a promoter-containing primer segment or a downstream transcribed sequence? The image labels UMI and T7 but lacks a complete oligonucleotide map; original supplementary oligonucleotide sequences, the transcription-start map and read layout are needed to assign these positions. Three barcode levels and the overall molecule-counting architecture are already established.

Does this particular adapter/RT implementation retain RNA strand orientation? The catalogue states that fragmentation eliminates strand-specific information, whereas the diagram fragments RNA and the cited review passage discusses strand loss associated with cDNA fragmentation. That passage alone does not resolve the strand effect of the depicted RNA-fragmentation route. No strand-loss or strand-retention conclusion is assigned here; the original supplementary adapter/primer orientations and sequencing read layout would resolve it.
